title: The vendored runtime names consumer projects, sessions and other repositories' commits, and ships no licence
body:
## Ask

From another estate's supervising session, on hv's instruction, 2026-10-03: the runtime devbin vendors into a project -- `bin/devbin` and everything under `bin/.devbin/lib/` -- must be truly generic. hv: "if devbin needs updating so that it is truly generic, then so be it", asking why a vendored install ever refers to projects that merely USE devbin. Some repositories are publishable to a client, and each vendors devbin 0.1.8 byte for byte under its manifest, so the fix is made here and reaches them through `devbin upgrade`.

## Measured at 6aa27b7 (vc)

Over the 73 files `vendored_paths` lists, 303 lines in 36 files name: thirteen consumer projects (146 lines in 26 files), whiteboard monikers (170 lines -- `hv's ruling`, `vc's N2`, `laksa/dc`, `target/cc`), commits (four from other repositories, four of devbin's own), one cross-estate issue (`utilz#0032`) and two home-directory paths. A further 20 lines name Intent as an estate rather than as the tool devbin drives; 16 name the tool and stay. Ten lines are live text rather than comments, among them `lib/infra.init:88`, which prints `(hv, 2026-09-08)` to the user, and `lib/pages/clean.md`, whose example directory is `target/cc`.

A word boundary cannot see a name glued to `_`, so a second census found eight more lines (`CONFLAB_ROOT`, `conflab_help`, three of them live YAML values), and the rewrite itself met leftovers no census held: another repository's tech note and crate names, Intent's shim, CI run ids, a dotfiles path, and `$HOME/Devel/opt/devbin` twice.

## hv's rulings, 2026-10-03

- A vendored devbin carries a licence file: Geodica Ltd (geodica.com), all rights reserved. A client that receives a project under an engagement "may use, copy and run that copy as part of that project" and takes no ownership.
- **devbin keeps no list of who uses it, in its runtime or in its tests.** hv: "Why would we need this list? That's an inverted dependency... Surely devbin doesn't give a hoot about projects that use it? If it does, then something is wrong." So the gate refuses by SHAPE, and a name in prose is held by review.
- The fix ships in the next release, and every change open by then is bundled into that one release.
- hv upgrades the estates as hv goes; there is no sweep.

## Done when

1. No file of the vendored runtime names a consumer project, the geodica estate, a whiteboard node, another repository's commit or issue, or a machine path. The reasoning in each comment stays, stated generically; the provenance stays in git, at the landing commit's parent.
2. Examples and help text use a neutral placeholder project, `demo`, the spelling `tests/unit/help.bats` already uses.
3. A suite gate refuses, by shape and with no list of who uses devbin, a commit, another repository's issue or CI run, a path on one machine, an attribution, and the owner's name off its copyright line, and has been watched to fail on each. It declares that a name in prose is review's to hold.
4. The vendored runtime carries `LICENSE.md` -- Geodica Ltd, all rights reserved, a client's use, copy and run as part of the delivered project -- and `bin/devbin`'s header carries the copyright line. The licence names its owner and no client.
5. It rides the next release, hv's bundle, and the session that asked for it is told that release's version and seam digest when it is cut. That last step is the cut's, carried on vc's board.

## Resolution

Landed at 6937d9e on cc's review: cc approved v1's rewrite, licence and rule line, and v2 is hv's two rulings applied -- the shape-only gate and the licence's use clause.

- Comments in 36 files rewritten so each keeps its lesson and drops who, where and when; `git show 6937d9e^:<path>` reads the old text. Live text: install's `--alias` help, infra.init's withheld-facet clause, `config.reference.yaml`'s example project (`demo`, `DEMO_*`, `web`), and `clean.md`'s per-session directory (`target/session-a`).
- `lib/LICENSE.md`, vendored as `bin/.devbin/lib/LICENSE.md`, and `bin/devbin`'s copyright line.
- `tests/unit/neutral.bats`: five arms, shape-only, each with a planted positive and an innocent negative control before the tree.
- `usage-rules.md` carries the rule, including that devbin keeps no list of who uses it.

Verified: 32 of the 34 changed shell files are code-same under `shfmt -mn`, and the two code diffs are the deliberate live-text lines. The full suite is green on v1 (2048 of 2048, seal 20261003-1640, .errors empty). After v2 was applied, the files that read the gate, the licence and the rule were re-run green (neutral, vendoredmd, helpers, contract, documentation, install, config and runwords: 329 of 329). neutral.bats is red on the original tree -- refs 12, paths 4, attribution 62, licence -- and green on this one. Eight mutants were each red on their own arm, and the results are identical under mawk and GNU grep, sed and coreutils.

Declared limits, each named in neutral.bats: a name in prose (review's); the manifest written beside the vendored set (0153); git history, here and in any consumer that vendored an earlier devbin; and a phrase split across two lines.
